messages:
Priya (PM): Heads-up — competitor X just announced an API-mode feature that mirrors our hosted endpoints (multipart response + tool-calling compatibility). We need to decide if and how this changes our Q2 roadmap.
Miguel (Eng): saw it. looks like mostly api-surface parity, not runtime optimizations. implementation risk depends on compatibility layer.
Sofia (Sales): several SEs already pinged me — a couple of enterprise prospects asked explicitly for that API shape. They said they'd pause evals until we support it.
Asha (Product Ops): important to quantify: how many existing customers would need it vs potential ARR upside? can sales enumerate top 5?
Sofia (Sales): yes — i'll DM the account list, but quick note: 2 deals > $250k are asking for the exact same contractable API shape.
Miguel (Eng): rough dev estimate: 3–4 sprints for a robust compatibility layer + tests and adapter code, maybe less if we ship a shim with documented limitations. Latency/regression risk if we add adapter in request path.
Jared (Design): if we do a shim, UX needs to clearly document behavior differences for function/tool calling and streaming. also need example snippets.
Priya (PM): options on the table:
- A: Full parity (API surface + behavior) — high dev cost, higher risk, satisfies sales asks
- B: Compatibility shim (partial) + focus on performance differentiators (latency, batching, cost) — lower immediate dev, preserves our differentiators
- C: Delay parity, push customers to dedicated/private where we can scope per-customer adapters — gates deals to larger contracts
Miguel (Eng): i'd prefer B. we can implement a lightweight adapter that maps incoming requests to our runtime and flag unsupported patterns. add telemetry to measure traffic and errors.
Asha (Product Ops): for B we should define launch criteria so sales can close confidently:
- documented adapter behavior + 4 example SDK snippets
- E2E smoke tests for streaming and tool-calls
- Perf regression < 10% on p95 latency for standard prompts
- Telemetry dashboard showing adapter errors and fallbacks
Sofia (Sales): that sounds workable if you commit to a canary timeline. sales needs a firm date to tell customers.
Priya (PM): proposed timeline: 2-week spike to validate adapter approach, then 4-sprint build if spike successful. Can we commit to spike start next Monday?
Miguel (Eng): yes, spike ok. will allocate 1 FE and 2 backend engs for 2 weeks. goal: prototype adapter + perf surface area.
Jared (Design): i'll draft the sample snippets and a short doc for the docs site during the spike.
Asha (Product Ops): I'll set up a lightweight eval plan: acceptance tests and canary rollout checklist.
Acceptance checklist draft:
- adapter v0 deployed to canary cluster
- smoke tests: streaming, tool-calls, kv-cache validity
- p95 latency measured and compared to baseline
- error rate < 1% on canary traffic
- docs + examples published
Sofia (Sales): also need an internal list of the top 3 accounts to offer canary access. i'll provide by EOD.
Priya (PM): decision for roadmap: start spike (B) next Monday. full parity (A) can be reconsidered after telemetry and customer demand from canary. If telemetry shows high usage and low risk, we'll prioritize full parity for the next planning cycle.
Miguel (Eng): one ask: provide a runbook for fallback behavior in case adapter causes 5xxs. Avoid cascading failures.
Asha (Product Ops): will add runbook + rollback steps to canary checklist.
LaunchBot: Meeting scheduled: "Adapter spike kickoff" on Mon 10:00am — invites sent.
Priya (PM): thanks all. action items:
- Miguel: spike team + prototype (owner)
- Jared: sample snippets + doc stub
- Asha: canary checklist + runbook
- Sofia: top 3 accounts for canary + deal impact notes
I'll update the roadmap ticket after spike outcome. Ping me in-thread for blockers. :thumbsup:
